paper_title: Effects of aerobic or resistance exercise on sleep and cancer-related fatigue in patients with breast cancer during or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: a 3-arm randomized controlled trial
design_rationale: The study explicitly used 1:1:1 blocked randomization with randomly varying block sizes, stratification by tumor type, and a computer-generated allocation list.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with randomly varying blocks and stratification, and allocation was concealed from recruiting staff until after baseline assessment; reported baseline differences do not provide clear evidence of randomization failure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A blocked randomization with randomly varying block size and stratified by tumor type ... was performed using a computer-generated randomization list. A biometrician, who was not involved in the recruitment of the participants, performed the allocation after completion of the baseline assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded, adherence was very low (about 26%–42%), and some early-intervention participants continued exercising after the assigned intervention, although the primary analyses estimated assignment effects using available randomized-group data and imputation included all randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blinding of participants for group allocation is not feasible in exercise intervention studies... participants in the AT group attended 41.6% of the sessions... RT group attended 40.6%... and participants in the WCG attended 25.8%.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missingness was substantial for key outcomes and differed modestly by participant characteristics, but completer comparisons suggested small symptom differences and multiple-imputation analyses of all 184 randomized participants were consistent with complete-case results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: PSQI global score: 27% missing at T2 and 30% at T3; EORTC QLQ-FA12 total fatigue: 13% at T2 and 20% at T3... pooled estimates closely matched the complete-case results.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated and consistently administered self-report and actigraphy measures were used, but participants were unblinded and the principal fatigue and subjective sleep outcomes could therefore have been influenced by knowledge of intervention assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Additionally, blinding of the participants was not possible due to the nature of the intervention and the self-reported outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: This was a secondary analysis with no prospective statistical analysis plan, the fatigue instrument was changed from the registered FAQ to EORTC QLQ-FA12, and many outcomes, time points, transformations, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were examined without global multiplicity correction, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No prospective statistical analysis plan was defined for the secondary outcomes reported in this manuscript... we initially focused on the Fatigue Assessment Questionnaire (FAQ)... [but] amended the CRF assessment accordingly... no global adjustments for multiple testing across outcomes or time points were applied.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by substantial risk of selective reporting in an unplanned secondary analysis with changed outcome measurement and extensive analytic multiplicity. Additional concerns arise from low adherence/crossover, substantial missing data, and unblinded self-reported outcomes.

paper_title: Feasibility of an exercise intervention for chemotherapy-related fatigue in patients with gynecologic cancer: a randomized controlled trial with multidimensional assessment
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized 1:1 using minimization through a web-based central randomization system with allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation used centrally administered minimization with stratification and concealment, and reported baseline characteristics were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were enrolled by the principal investigators at each site, and randomization was performed using minimization within the UMIN Internet Data and Information system for Clinical and Epidemiological research, Cloud version (INDICE cloud)... This web-based central randomization system ensured allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded, control-group activity was strongly altered or contaminated (71% met the exercise criterion), and the analysis excluded randomized participants without post-baseline primary-outcome assessment rather than following a strict intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Notably, 71% of participants in the control group, despite receiving no formal exercise prescription, exceeded the same criteria.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome analysis omitted four of 55 exercise participants and used complete cases, with three withdrawals and one post-enrollment ineligibility all occurring in that group; the limited and imbalanced missingness could plausibly introduce some bias, although its extent was small.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the exercise group, three patients withdrew consent, and one was deemed ineligible after enrollment, resulting in 51 evaluable cases... Missing data were handled with a complete-case approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: FACIT-F is an appropriate validated measure administered consistently with responses shielded from treating physicians, but the primary outcome was self-reported by unblinded participants who could have expectations about exercise benefits.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: PROs were completed on paper forms and sealed by the patients themselves before being submitted in envelopes to the administrative staff at the reception desk, ensuring that responses were not accessible to the treating physicians.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary endpoint was clearly defined, but no protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided to verify the reported covariate-adjusted analysis, complete-case choices, and selection among repeated FACIT-F measurements and multiple analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was defined as the change in fatigue, assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy–Fatigue (FACIT-F) subscale... from baseline to the end of chemotherapy.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because severe control-group contamination represented a major deviation from the assigned interventions and the analysis was not strictly intention-to-treat. Additional concerns arise from complete-case exclusions, unblinded self-reported fatigue measurement, and insufficient information to exclude selective reporting.

paper_title: Effects of high-intensity interval training compared with resistance training in prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a randomized controlled trial
design_rationale: Although the title labels the study a randomized controlled trial, the supplied text contains only references and does not explicitly describe a random allocation method in a Methods/Participants section; per the prespecified rule, randomization cannot be assumed.

domain_judgments.rationale: The supplied material contains no Methods, participant characteristics, baseline comparisons, or adjusted analyses, so comparability of the intervention groups cannot be assessed.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: No eligibility, recruitment, enrollment, or condition-assignment procedures are provided, preventing assessment of whether selection was related to intervention and outcome.

The title clearly identifies the compared conditions as high-intensity interval training and resistance training, but the supplied text gives no operational definitions or information about consistent classification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Effects of high-intensity interval training compared with resistance training in prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a randomized controlled trial

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: There is no information on intervention adherence, co-interventions, participant awareness, protocol deviations, crossover, or the analysis population.
Participant flow, attrition, missing outcome proportions, reasons for missingness, and methods for handling missing data are not reported in the supplied material.

The references suggest use of established instruments for fatigue, quality of life, depression, sleep, and walking capacity, but the supplied text does not identify the analyzed outcome, assessment procedures, or assessor blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Measuring fatigue and other anemia-related symptoms with the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy (FACT) measurement system.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol, registration, prespecified analysis plan, outcomes, analyses, or study results are supplied, so selective reporting cannot be assessed.

overall_summary: The supplied text is only a reference list and does not provide the Methods, participant flow, outcome assessment, or results needed for a ROBINS-I assessment. Intervention labels and citations permit limited inference in two domains, but the principal bias domains remain unassessable.

paper_title: Resistance Training, Fatigue, Quality of Life, Anxiety in Breast Cancer Survivors
design_rationale: The abstract explicitly describes the study as a randomized controlled trial and states that the 25 women were randomized to resistance-training or control groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is stated, but the sequence-generation method, allocation concealment, and baseline group comparability are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomized controlled trial. The 25 women included were randomized into RT or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily could know whether they performed resistance training, while adherence, unintended deviations, contamination, and whether all randomized participants were analyzed in their assigned groups are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The RT group performed eight weeks of RT (once per week).

domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract reports that 25 women were included but does not state how many completed follow-up or were included in the outcome analyses, so the extent and impact of missing data cannot be established.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 25 women included were randomized into RT or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Quality of life was measured consistently with the SF-36, an appropriate questionnaire, but this participant-reported outcome could be influenced by unavoidable knowledge of exercise assignment and no blinding safeguards are described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Quality of life was evaluated using the SF-36 questionnaire.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and only four statistically significant SF-36 subscales are presented despite eight measured domains and multiple stated statistical tests, creating substantial risk of selective outcome or analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The results show resistance training improved the following subscales of SF-36: aspects of physical functioning (+27%, p = 0.027), physical role functioning (+54%, p=0.008), emotional role functioning (+42%, p=0,027) and metal health (+16%, p=0,032).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because selective reporting is strongly suspected: only significant results from four of eight SF-36 domains are presented without a protocol or prespecified analysis plan. Additional concerns arise from absent details on allocation concealment, adherence and analysis population, attrition, and blinding.

paper_title: Effect of Tai Chi and Resistance Training on Cancer-Related Fatigue and Quality of Life in Middle-Aged and Elderly Cancer Patients
design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 120 patients were randomly assigned to four groups using a random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random number table was used, but allocation concealment and baseline comparability are not reported in the available text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Totally 120 cancer patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to 4 groups by a random number table

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew which exercise condition they received, and the available text does not report adherence, crossovers, intervention-related deviations, or whether an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants in the TC group received 24-form simplified Yang-style TC training at a frequency of 40 min per day, 3 days per week for 12 weeks. Patients in the two RT groups received 10 sessions, 6 designated movements per day, 3 days per week for 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The available report gives the initial sample size but does not state how many participants completed follow-up or whether missing outcome data and attrition were handled appropriately.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Totally 120 cancer patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to 4 groups

domain_judgments.rationale: The fatigue and quality-of-life outcomes were measured with established questionnaires consistently across groups, but they were self-reported by participants who could not be blinded to exercise assignment, allowing knowledge of intervention to influence responses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The scores of Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI), QoL questionnaire for Chinese cancer patients receiving chemobiotherapy (QLQ-CCC), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were measured before and after training.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, while numerous outcomes and group comparisons were assessed, creating scope for selective reporting among eligible measurements or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 1-RM of 6 muscle groups, fat mass (FM), lean body mass (LBM), along with the scores of Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI), QLQ-CCC, GAD-7, PHQ-9 and PSQI were measured before and after training.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Although random assignment by a random number table was reported, allocation concealment, attrition, adherence and analysis population were insufficiently described, and unblinded self-reported outcomes plus the absence of a prespecified analysis plan raise additional concerns.

paper_title: Improvements in muscle strength, power, and size and self-reported fatigue as mediators of the effect of resistance exercise on physical performance breast cancer survivor women: a randomized controlled trial
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that 26 eligible breast cancer survivors were randomized to control or resistance-exercise groups using MedCalc's 'Create random group' tool.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computerized random-group tool was used, but allocation concealment was not described and the very small groups showed potentially important baseline differences (including age and fatigue) despite nonsignificant tests.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used the tool of Medcalc® (Create random group) to assign cases to random groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention staff necessarily knew whether resistance exercise or stretching was received, and the analysis excluded six post-randomization dropouts rather than following intention-to-treat, creating potential bias from intervention-related deviations and adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the intervention, six women dropped out (health and personal problems) (Figure 1). All selected volunteers (CT: n = 09 and RE: n = 11) performed self-reported fatigue, body composition, MS, MP, and PP at the beginning and the end of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were unavailable for 6 of 26 randomized participants (23%), with differential attrition implied by final group sizes of 9/13 versus 11/13, and no sensitivity analysis established that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the intervention, six women dropped out (health and personal problems) (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The physical-performance outcomes were objective, standardized, and generally reliable, but assessor blinding was not reported and encouragement or timing could be influenced by knowledge of group assignment; self-reported fatigue was also susceptible to unblinded expectations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All voluntaries were verbally encouraged to maintain a maximum velocity walk. All tests were assessed in duplicate and the shortest walking time was used to calculate walking speed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered, no prespecified protocol or analysis plan is provided for comparison, and many eligible performance outcomes and mediator correlations were analyzed, leaving scope for selective reporting despite a stated MANOVA correction.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To determine whether the changes in SRF, LBM.L, MS, and PMax were associated with the change in PP tests (10M.UWT, 10M.FWT, 5STS, TUG, 30STS, 400MWT, 6MWT and 1MILEWT), we used a coefficient of correlations adopting a within-subject model.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the complete-case rather than intention-to-treat analysis and substantial post-randomization missing outcome data (6/26 participants). Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment and assessor blinding, as well as multiplicity and possible selective reporting across numerous outcomes and mediator analyses.

paper_title: Progressive resistance training in cachectic head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a randomized controlled pilot feasibility trial
design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random allocation of 20 participants to progressive resistance training or usual care using blocked randomization and sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blocked randomization and sealed envelopes were reported, but the method used to generate the sequence and safeguards ensuring opaque, sequentially numbered envelopes were not described; nevertheless, reported baseline characteristics were broadly balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were allocated at random to the control or exercise group via blocked randomization in sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists could not be blinded, intervention delivery was sometimes adjusted, control participants could receive physiotherapy, and no intention-to-treat analysis was explicitly specified, although all randomized participants completed follow-up and strengthening was excluded from usual care.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The small sample size and non-blinding of assessors and therapists are major limitations which reflect lack of time and budget in pilot studies.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 20 randomized participants completed the trial, indicating outcome data were available for essentially all participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All included patients were randomized into intervention and control groups before beginning RT. The completion rate was 100%.

domain_judgments.rationale: The same coordinator performed all assessments but was explicitly unblinded, and several outcomes were subjective self-reports or effort-/tester-dependent physical tests, making differential measurement influenced by intervention knowledge plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The present pilot study has certain limitations. The small sample size and non-blinding of assessors and therapists are major limitations

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered retrospectively, numerous outcomes, subscales, time points, and analytic contrasts were available, and no prespecified analysis plan is reported, creating substantial scope for selective reporting of favorable trends.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Registered 15 May 2018 - Retrospectively registered.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because outcome assessors were unblinded for subjective and assessor-dependent outcomes, and retrospective registration combined with multiple outcomes, time points, and analyses creates substantial risk of selective result reporting. There were also some concerns about allocation concealment details and deviations/analysis, although follow-up was complete.

paper_title: Effects of a 6-Week Supervised Multimodal Exercise Program on Cancer-Related Fatigue, Quality of Life and Physical Function During Active Treatment: A Randomized Controlled Trial
design_rationale: This was a parallel-group randomized controlled trial in which 110 participants were allocated 1:1 using a computer-generated sequence created in Microsoft Excel by an independent researcher.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated by an independent researcher, concealed from recruiters until eligibility and baseline assessment were complete, and reported baseline characteristics were broadly balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to the supervised therapeutic exercise group or the control group using a computer-generated sequence created with Microsoft Excel by an independent researcher, who maintained custody of the allocation list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded and the supervised group received substantially more attention than controls, creating potential behavior-related deviations or contamination, although adherence was high, there were no intervention-related withdrawals, and all participants were analyzed as randomized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, blinding of participants was not feasible.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 110 randomized participants completed the six-week outcome assessment, so no outcome data were missing and the ITT analysis included every randomized participant.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 110 randomized participants, all completed the post intervention assessment at six weeks; therefore, no losses to follow-up were recorded, and the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis included all 110 participants in their originally assigned groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated outcomes were administered consistently and outcome assessment was reportedly blinded, but the unblinded participants self-reported the primary fatigue and quality-of-life outcomes and could plausibly have been influenced by intervention awareness and unequal attention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, participant blinding was not feasible, which may have influenced self-reported outcomes, despite the allocation concealment and blinding implemented at key stages of the process.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and identifies two main outcomes with baseline-adjusted ANCOVA, but the supplied report does not establish that a prospective protocol or statistical analysis plan fixed all outcome scales, responder thresholds, subgroup analyses, and analytic choices before unblinded data were available.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition to the primary ANCOVA analyses, exploratory responder analyses were conducted to support clinical interpretability.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Randomization, allocation concealment, complete follow-up, and ITT analysis were strong, but participant non-blinding and unequal attention could influence self-reported primary outcomes, and prospective prespecification of all reported analyses was not fully demonstrated.

paper_title: The impact of maximal strength training on quality of life among women with breast cancer undergoing treatment
design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that the 57 patients were randomized into training and control groups, although the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study states that participants were randomized and reported broadly similar baseline characteristics, but it gives no information on sequence generation or allocation concealment, and treatment proportions differed somewhat between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized into a TG and CG.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention providers necessarily knew group assignment, the control group received motivational calls and prescribed chair stands rather than purely standard care, and the analysis included only completers rather than clearly following intention-to-treat, although adherence was high and deviations were limited.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, 55 patients (N = 27 in TG, N = 28 in CG) completed the entire program.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2 of 57 randomized participants (3.5%) dropped out for family or work circumstances, leaving outcome data for nearly all participants with reasons unlikely to depend on outcome values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the intervention period 2 patients dropped out (mean age 52 years) due to family or work circumstances.

domain_judgments.rationale: Quality of life was measured consistently with validated EORTC questionnaires, but it was participant-reported and participants were aware of assignment, so responses could have been influenced by knowledge of receiving supervised exercise; the paper does not report blinded outcome assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measure was the QoL measured by The European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality of Life Questionnaire-C30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) and additional BC Module (QLQ-BR23).

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or preregistered analysis plan is reported, numerous eligible questionnaire scales and analyses were available, and only selected QLQ-C30 and QLQ-BR23 results are tabulated or discussed despite the instruments containing many more scales and items, creating substantial scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The QLQ-C30 is composed of multi-item scales and single-item measures. These include 5 functional scales, 3 symptom scales, a global health status/QoL scale, and 6 single items.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because selective outcome/result reporting is likely: no prespecified protocol is cited and only a subset of the many measured questionnaire outcomes is presented. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, completer-only analysis, and unblinded self-reported quality-of-life outcomes.

paper_title: Quality of Life, Fatigue, and Sleep Problems in Pancreatic Cancer Patients: A Randomized Trial on the Effects of Exercise
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned using a 2:1 block-randomization sequence generated with a random number generator, stratified by sex and age, with assignment performed by an independent biometrician.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random sequence with stratification, varying blocks, and independent assignment was described, but concealment until enrollment was not explicitly stated and geographic eligibility determined which exercise arm a participant could enter, with some baseline imbalances in this small sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A 2:1 block randomization, stratified by sex and age, with a random number generator and varying block sizes of 3 and 6 was used. Randomization of a patient was done by an independent biometrician according to the pre-specified allocation list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and some personnel were necessarily unblinded, exercise adherence declined substantially, and the primary complete-case analysis excluded randomized participants without analyzable six-month data despite assignment being modeled by intention-to-treat; however, usual care controls were advised not to change exercise and sensitivity analyses used multiple imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary dataset included all patients for which analyzable data were available after 6 months (complete–case analysis).

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 47 of 65 randomized participants completed six months, with differential dropout up to 32.3%, and the primary analysis was complete case; moreover, the imputation excluded patients whose death or progression prevented participation, making outcome-dependent missingness plausible in this severe disease.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 47 patients completed the intervention period... Data for patients who died or had disease progression, preventing further participation, within 6 months, were not substituted during the multiple imputation procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated questionnaires were administered consistently across groups, but outcomes were participant-reported and participants could not be blinded to an exercise intervention, so knowledge of assignment could influence subjective quality-of-life, fatigue, and sleep ratings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures were collected via self-reported questionnaires prior to the intervention (T0, baseline), at mid-intervention (T1, after 3 months) and post-intervention (T2, after 6 months).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and identified six-month physical functioning as primary, but numerous secondary scales, time points, pooled and separate-group contrasts, adjustments, and exploratory three-month analyses created substantial multiplicity, while the supplied report does not establish that all analyses were prespecified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition, comparisons of the pooled resistance training group (RT), combining RT1 and RT2, with CON were conducted as exploratory analyses... Similar exploratory analyses were performed for all secondary endpoints.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven principally by substantial and plausibly outcome-dependent missing data handled primarily through complete-case analysis, with deaths and progression not imputed. Additional concerns arise from imperfectly documented allocation concealment, declining adherence and lack of a full ITT analysis, unblinded self-reported outcomes, and extensive exploratory analyses.

paper_title: Effect of home-based resistance training on chemotherapy relative dose intensity and tolerability in colon cancer: The FORCE randomized control trial
design_rationale: The study explicitly used 1:1 covariate-adaptive random allocation through the web-based QMinim system to assign 181 participants to resistance training or usual care.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a web-based covariate-adaptive procedure and baseline characteristics were largely balanced, but the report does not explicitly state that the allocation sequence was concealed until assignment or describe the random component of minimization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized by the study manager and enrolled by the field interviewers to the resistance training, or usual care group in a 1 to 1 ratio using QMinim, a web based adaption of MinimPy, a covariate adaptive randomization procedure

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded in this behavioral trial, intervention adherence was lower than prescribed, delivery changed to tele-coaching during COVID-19, and the report does not explicitly identify the analysis as intention-to-treat, although analyses were based on assigned group and nearly all randomized participants were included for RDI.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants randomized to the resistance training group completed a median of 1.4 (0.6–1.7) sessions per week, using a weight that was 62% (53–70) of the estimated one-repetition maximum

domain_judgments.rationale: RDI was available for 180 of 181 randomized participants, but only 77% of expected patient-reported toxicity forms were returned and the missing-at-random assumption was not empirically established, despite similar completion between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seventy-seven percent of the expected number of PRO-CTCAE forms were returned and there were no differences in completion rate between resistance training (74%) and usual care (81%).

domain_judgments.rationale: RDI was objectively calculated using a standard formula and PRO-CTCAE is an appropriate validated measure applied similarly across groups, but participants necessarily knew their assignment and could therefore have influenced self-reported symptom outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To assess toxicities, nine symptoms specific to side effects of chemotherapy for colon cancer were measured using Patient-Reported Outcomes version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE).

domain_judgments.rationale: The co-primary outcomes, planned cut points, and several subgroup analyses are described as prespecified, but no trial registration or accessible prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported here to exclude selective choice among analyses, and multiple secondary and exploratory analyses were conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We conducted analyses stratified by a priori planned subgroups (treatment duration, sex, frailty status), and exploratory subgroups (age, randomization before or after chemotherapy start).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The principal issues are incomplete reporting of allocation concealment and prespecification, lack of participant blinding with self-reported toxicity outcomes, incomplete PRO-CTCAE follow-up, and imperfect intervention adherence, although the objective RDI outcome was nearly complete and analyzed by assigned group.

paper_title: Exploring the feasibility of exercise training during (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy in women with early-stage breast cancer: a pilot study examining immune and metabolic outcomes.
design_rationale: The study explicitly describes itself as non-randomised; participants self-selected into an intervention and a convenience control group was recruited after no eligible participants chose usual care.

domain_judgments.rationale: Self-selection, convenience controls, baseline menopausal differences, heterogeneous chemotherapy, and systematically different blood-sampling conditions create major uncontrolled confounding, with no multivariable adjustment or matching used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants self-selected into the exercise intervention, introducing the potential for selection bias... baseline differences in menopausal status between groups, which limit between-group comparability and preclude causal inference.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Condition membership was determined by participant preference and subsequent convenience recruitment, likely selecting exercisers who were more motivated and able to participate and controls through a different process related to intervention uptake and potentially outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were informed about the study interventions and self-selected into either the supervised exercise or FMD intervention according to their preference. As no eligible participants opted for the usual-care control group, a convenience sample of control participants was subsequently recruited.

domain_judgments.rationale: Exercise and usual-care control conditions were clearly defined before outcome assessment, and supervised attendance and adherence records made misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants completed a 12-week supervised combined aerobic and resistance training programme (~ 60 min per session)... The programme was designed to include two supervised sessions during chemotherapy weeks and three sessions during non-chemotherapy weeks.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew their intervention, exercise exposure was flexibly modified by symptoms and medical issues, and analyses included only the 11 intervention completers rather than all 13 enrolled, although modifications and adherence were documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The remaining eleven patients (84.6% retention rate) completed the 12-week programme and were included in the analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Two of 13 exercise participants withdrew and were excluded, whereas the six controls appear to have provided biomarker data; the withdrawals were attributed to travel but no sensitivity analysis assessed possible bias from their missing outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients withdrew from the exercise intervention due to travel-related reasons... The remaining eleven patients (84.6% retention rate) completed the 12-week programme and were included in the analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment differed materially by group: exercise blood samples were fasting while control samples were non-fasting, sampling timing relative to chemotherapy and follow-up intervals differed, and patient-reported/body-composition outcomes lacked control measurements; assessor blinding was not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the control group, due to logistical constraints related to chemotherapy scheduling, blood samples were not collected in a fasting state... with intervals between baseline and post-intervention sampling ranging from 3 to 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: Numerous immune, metabolic, body-composition, and patient-reported outcomes were tested without multiplicity correction, results with P<0.10 were emphasized as signals, and outcome-dependent exploratory post-hoc within-group analyses were performed, creating substantial scope for selective emphasis despite trial registration.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Given that this pilot trial was underpowered by design, both statistically significant differences (p < 0.05) and signals toward statistical significance (p < 0.10) are reported. Within-group analyses were restricted to markers showing between-group differences or signals and were considered exploratory post-hoc analyses.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by self-selection and convenience recruitment, substantial uncontrolled confounding, group-specific blood collection and outcome assessment, and selective-analysis/reporting concerns. Moderate risks from intervention deviations and missing outcomes further weaken causal interpretation.

paper_title: Effects of Resistance Exercise on Symptoms, Physical Function, and Quality of Life in Gastrointestinal Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemotherapy
design_rationale: Allocation was explicitly quasi-random and based on the order in which patients presented for evaluation, not on a random sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assignment by presentation order was predictable and potentially associated with temporal or clinical prognostic factors, while analyses were unadjusted; measured baseline characteristics appeared similar but do not exclude residual confounding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants were quasi-randomized into 2 groups according to the order they came for evaluation: resistance exercise group and relaxation control group.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: All participants came from one hospital and eligibility required willingness and capacity to complete exercise, but condition allocation followed recruitment and there is no clear evidence that inclusion after assignment depended jointly on intervention and outcome risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the participants in this research were recruited from Quanzhou First Hospital Affiliated to Fujian Medical University.

domain_judgments.rationale: The resistance-exercise and relaxation-control interventions were clearly defined and assigned prospectively, making misclassification unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Machine-based resistance exercise was performed twice a week for 12 weeks under the guidance of experienced therapists.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew whether strengthening exercise was delivered, adherence and unintended co-interventions were insufficiently reported, and only completers rather than all assigned participants were analyzed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, 94 participants in the resistance exercise group and 96 in the relaxation control group finished the research and their data were recorded and analyzed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for 14 of 204 assigned participants (6.9%), with slightly differential attrition and no reasons, sensitivity analysis, or evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During this research, 8 participants in the resistance exercise group and 6 in the relaxation control group were lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although researchers collecting data were reportedly blinded, participants knew their intervention and several key symptom and quality-of-life outcomes were self-reported and therefore readily influenced by intervention awareness; resistance-trained participants also had direct familiarity with strength-testing tasks.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The QoL of the patients were analyzed through the administration of European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-C30 (EORTC QLQ-C30).

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: Many symptoms, physical tests, questionnaire subscales, time contrasts, and statistical tests were available, but no prospective analysis plan is presented and reporting emphasizes nominally significant findings without multiplicity control.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis was significant when P value <.05.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is serious, driven by nonrandom order-based allocation with inadequate control of confounding, awareness-sensitive outcome measurement, and substantial analytical/reporting flexibility across numerous outcomes. Moderate concerns also remain about selection, deviations from intended interventions, and missing data.

paper_title: Quality of Life and Fatigue of Patients With Spinal Bone Metastases Under Combined Treatment With Resistance Training and Radiation Therapy: A Randomized Pilot Trial
design_rationale: The supplied full text is a single-patient case report in which clinicians selected transduodenal local excision based on tumor characteristics; it describes no random allocation or comparator group, notwithstanding the mismatched randomized-trial title.

domain_judgments.rationale: This uncontrolled single-patient case report cannot separate the effect of transduodenal local excision from the patient's clinical characteristics, co-interventions, perioperative care, or natural course, and no confounding control was possible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Considering the size, the position and absence of malignancy we decided to proceed to transduodenal local excision of the adenoma.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: The report presents one clinically selected patient without eligibility criteria, a sampling frame, or evidence that the case was representative, making intervention- and outcome-related case selection likely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study we present a case of a 78-year-old Greek man who was diagnosed with adenoma of the ampulla of Vater.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention received was directly documented and described in sufficient procedural detail, so misclassification is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The operation consisted of transduodenal local excision of the adenoma of the ampulla of Vater, sphincterotomy of Oddi, followed by Oddi sphincteroplasty, exploration of his common bile duct and gastrointestinal anastomosis.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The procedure and major accompanying surgical components were reported, but there was no prespecified protocol or systematic information about adherence and other perioperative co-interventions, so unintended deviations cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally a Kehr tube was placed in his common bile duct through the incision of the exploration. The gastrointestinal anastomosis was conducted to reduce the inner pressure at his duodenum.

domain_judgments.rationale: Immediate postoperative findings and discharge were reported, but no longer-term follow-up was provided despite recurrence being clinically important, leaving relevant outcome data missing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: He was discharged after a total of 16 days in our hospital.

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective postoperative cholangiography, laboratory testing, and histology reduce measurement concerns, but outcomes were not prespecified and were assessed by the treating team without blinded or independent assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One week later a postoperative cholangiography revealed no obstructions of his biliary tree and the results of his biochemical blood tests were normal.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: There was no protocol or prespecified analysis, and the narrative selectively reported favorable short-term outcomes while omitting systematic adverse-event and long-term recurrence assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Transduodenal local excision of the ampulla of Vater has limited side effects and postoperative complications, suggesting this particular technique to be the proper treatment for nonmalignant cases of adenomas.

overall_summary: Overall ROBINS-I risk is critical because this is an uncontrolled, clinically selected single-patient case report with critical confounding bias. Serious participant-selection and selective-reporting concerns, together with absent long-term follow-up, further preclude a reliable causal estimate of treatment effect.

paper_title: The effects of home-based exercise therapy for breast cancer-related fatigue induced by radical radiotherapy.
design_rationale: This was a two-arm randomized controlled trial in which 106 women were allocated 1:1 to home-based exercise or usual care using balanced randomization stratified by treatment history and age.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was stratified and performed by a researcher without participant contact, but the method used to generate the random sequence and the mechanism ensuring concealment until enrollment were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Balanced randomization procedures were utilized to allocate participants into the two study arms at a ratio of 1:1 stratified for treatment history... and age... Randomization was conducted by a researcher who had no contact with participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew their assignment, adherence was substantially below the exercise target, controls were permitted to exercise, and the analysis population of 89 completers rather than all 106 randomized participants suggests no intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eighty-nine (84%) participants completed the study (exercise = 43, usual care = 46)... The usual care group did not receive any recommendation or support to exercise but were not advised or requested to change their exercise behavior or avoid exercise.

domain_judgments.rationale: Seventeen of 106 randomized participants (16%) withdrew, including withdrawals due to difficulty coping with treatment and burden of questionnaires/logbooks, and no sensitivity analysis or other evidence was provided to show that missingness could not bias the outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 17 participants withdrew from the study (exercise = 8, usual care = 9), due to (a) difficulty coping with treatment (n = 3), (b) finding the filling of questionnaires and logbook burdensome (n = 4), (c) due to personal reasons (n = 9), and (d) one patient in the usual care group died.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary fatigue instruments were validated and administered on the same schedule across groups, but fatigue was self-reported by participants who could not be blinded and whose responses could plausibly be influenced by assignment and additional intervention contact.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Cancer-related fatigue was assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F) questionnaire... Validity and reliability of the measurement tool has been established.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration number is reported, but the text does not establish that outcomes and analyses were prospectively prespecified; fatigue had two instruments and many time points, and the achieved-power calculation used a one-tailed design, leaving potential for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants had completed a written informed consent and medical questionnaire approved by the institution’s human research ethics committee before participating in the study (ANZCTR registration number: ACTRN12611001266954).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The study was randomized and attrition was balanced, but sequence generation/concealment were incompletely described, analyses appeared restricted to completers, 16% of randomized participants withdrew, outcomes were unblinded self-reports, and prospective prespecification of the numerous outcome analyses was unclear.

paper_title: Exercise Training Benefits Health-Related Quality of Life and Functional Capacity during Breast Cancer Chemotherapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that 93 women were randomly allocated to supervised exercise plus usual care or usual care alone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation is stated, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods and evidence about baseline balance are not reported in the available text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety-three women with early-stage BC were randomly allocated to a SETP plus usual care (exercise, n = 47) or usual care alone (UC, n = 46).

domain_judgments.rationale: The behavioral intervention precluded participant blinding, and adherence, contamination, and other deviations are not described, although an intention-to-treat approach was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mean changes from baseline were assessed by an intention-to-treat approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: The available text does not report retention, the amount or distribution of missing outcome data, or assumptions used to handle missing observations, so bias from missingness cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mean changes from baseline were assessed by an intention-to-treat approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated HRQoL questionnaires and standard functional tests were administered at common time points, but participant-reported outcomes were necessarily unblinded and assessor blinding for performance tests is not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EORTC Cancer Quality-of-Life-Questionnaire-Core-30 (QLQ-C30) and the BC-specific module (QLQ-BR23) were used to assess HRQoL. Functional capacity was analyzed by maximum voluntary handgrip strength (MVHS) and by the 30-s chair sit-to-stand test (30-s CST).

domain_judgments.rationale: Numerous HRQoL domains, functional outcomes, and time points were analyzed, while no preregistration, protocol, or prespecified analysis plan is reported in the available text to rule out selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: These endpoints were assessed at baseline (t0); middle (t1; after 8 or 12 wk of t0); and at the end of chemotherapy (t2; after 20 wk of t0).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. Although the study reports random allocation and intention-to-treat analysis, the available text lacks details on sequence concealment, baseline balance, adherence and deviations, missing outcomes, assessor blinding, and prespecification of outcomes and analyses.

paper_title: A Randomized Controlled 'REAL-FITNESS' Trial to Evaluate Physical Activity in Patients With Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma.
design_rationale: This was a parallel-group randomized controlled trial with centralized electronic allocation using a computer-generated random list prepared by a trial assistant who was not involved in enrollment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was explicitly computer-generated, centrally implemented through a web-based system, and created by an assistant uninvolved in enrollment; although some baseline differences occurred, these are plausible in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was centralized and performed electronically with the use of a Web-based response system. Patients were randomly assigned to the exercise or control group using a computer-generated random list created by a trial assistant who was not involved in the enrolment process.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and trainers could not be blinded to this behavioral intervention, and the efficacy analyses excluded two randomized exercise participants for nonadherence rather than using intention-to-treat, creating a substantial risk that intervention effects were biased.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This way, two patients who did not fulfil WHO recommendations through additional training at home were identified and excluded from the final analysis. This may be criticized, as it does not respect the intention-to-treat principle.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome analyses omitted 2 of 34 randomized participants (5.9%), both from the exercise arm and specifically because their post-randomization adherence was low, making missingness plausibly related to both intervention receipt and outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients did not fulfil WHO recommendations throughout the study period (adherence in intervention group: 16/18; 89%); ... a total of 32 patients were included into the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Several key outcomes were participant-reported or involved assessor judgment, participants necessarily knew their assigned group, and assessor blinding was not reported, so knowledge of allocation could plausibly influence measurements such as fatigue, quality of life, depression, TUGT, and treatment-related decisions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We compared ... fatigue, depression ... ‘timed-up-and-go-test’ (TUGT), Revised Myeloma Comorbidity Index (R-MCI), QoL (SF-12 questionnaire) ... in exercise vs. control cohorts.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and endpoints were described, but no prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided, while many outcomes, repeated time points, and alternative analysis methods were available, leaving scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Demographics, osteolytic lesions, infections, fatigue, depression, and biomarkers ... were compared ... (13 tests at baseline, during VCd and end of treatment [EOT]).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by exclusion of two randomized nonadherent exercise participants from the final analysis and the resulting outcome-data concern. Lack of blinding for subjective or assessor-influenced outcomes and flexibility across numerous outcomes and analyses add further risk.

paper_title: A randomised controlled trial comparing the effects of a 12-week supervised exercise versus usual care on outcomes in haematological cancer patients
design_rationale: The abstract explicitly states that 37 patients were randomly assigned to exercise rehabilitation or usual care, so the study is classified as randomized despite the absence of sequence-generation details in the available text.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is explicitly reported, but the available text does not describe sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline comparability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-seven patients (49 % recruitment rate) were randomly assigned to the 12-week exercise rehabilitation (n = 18) or usual care (n = 19).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received supervised exercise or usual care, and although adherence was high and no withdrawals occurred, the available text does not report deviations, contamination, or whether an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were given tailored exercise programmes comprising aerobic and resistance exercises, carried out three times per week for 12 weeks in local gyms and clinics.

domain_judgments.rationale: The report states that there were no study withdrawals, indicating outcome data were likely available for nearly all randomized participants, although item-level missingness is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There were no adverse reactions or study withdrawals.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes appear to have been measured using established self-report and objective instruments, but participant blinding was impossible for self-reported fatigue and quality of life and assessor blinding is not reported, allowing knowledge of allocation to influence some measurements.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pre-, post- and follow-up assessments were conducted on outcome measures including CRF, quality of life (QoL), psychological distress, cardiovascular fitness, muscle strength (MS) and body composition.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, which reduces concern, but the available text reports numerous outcomes and does not provide a protocol or prespecified analysis plan sufficient to verify that measurements and analyses were selected without flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12609000450213.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main limitations are absent details about allocation concealment and analysis, unavoidable participant awareness with subjective outcomes, unreported assessor blinding, and insufficient information to rule out selective reporting; no withdrawals lowers concern about missing data.

paper_title: Resistance exercise in men receiving androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer
design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly allocated to resistance exercise or waiting-list control using a table of random numbers, with stratification by center and treatment intent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated with a random-number table, allocation was concealed through baseline assessment and stratification, and reported baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization, performed using a table of random numbers, was stratified according to center (Ottawa or Edmonton) and intent of treatment (curative or palliative)... The treatment allocation was concealed from the study coordinator until completion of baseline testing and stratification.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were unblinded in a behavioral intervention with substantially greater attention in the exercise arm, and although an intention-to-treat analysis was used, adherence averaged 79% and baseline observation carried forward was used for dropouts rather than a more robust missing-data method.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No blinding of patients was used in treatment group assignment, and they were immediately informed about their group assignment... Attendance at the prescribed resistance exercise sessions averaged 79% (28 of 36 sessions).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were missing for 12.9% overall, with somewhat more dropout in control than intervention, and missing outcomes were replaced by baseline values using last observation carried forward, which can bias change estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the intervention period, eight men (9.8%) dropped out in the intervention group compared with 12 men (16.4%) in the control group... Overall, end-of-treatment (12-week) data were available for 135 of 155 men (87.1%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes were self-reported fatigue and quality of life, and participants necessarily knew whether they were receiving supervised exercise or waiting-list control, so outcome reports could plausibly be influenced by treatment awareness and differential attention despite blinded scoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were fatigue and health-related quality of life... No blinding of patients was used in treatment group assignment, and they were immediately informed about their group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes and planned subgroup factors were identified a priori, but no protocol or prospective registration is reported and each multidimensional questionnaire permitted potentially multiple eligible scores or analyses, so selective reporting cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were fatigue and health-related quality of life. Secondary outcomes were muscular fitness and body composition.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the primary outcomes being participant-reported in an unblinded exercise-versus-wait-list comparison with substantial differential attention. Additional concerns arise from 12.9% missing follow-up data handled by baseline observation carried forward and the absence of a reported prospective protocol or registration.
